analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md changed (docs-only). It adds a v0.9.21 candidate section and renames the v0.9.20 heading. It describes security-relevant behavior that is not in this diff and cannot be verified from it.

1) Dev provider identity: separate paths, labels, keychain items, a separate encrypted KV cache directory (darkbloom-dev/kv3), and ports. This touches T-041 (cache storage and at-rest scope) and A-003/A-008 (key and token custody). The next pass should check that the dev kv3 root cannot share a KEK or lookup-key namespace with production, and that the cache write-budget ledger stays per install.

2) Automatic dev release publication on push to master (build, sign, notarize). This is a release-integrity and signing-key (A-005/A-011) concern. The changelog says dev runs never receive PROD_* secrets. A reviewer must verify in the workflow files, which are not in this diff, that dev-signed artifacts cannot register hashes in the production registry or be accepted by the production coordinator or App Attest qualification (A-017, T-054).

3) OOM detection now matches the exact process name 'darkbloom'. This is an availability and watchdog detail (T-043).

4) Fan helper v2 keeps one lease per provider session. Version-downgrade refusal relates to T-044/T-047.

5) Startup health-check timing and throughput bootstrap affect routing evidence only (T-007 adjacent).

No threat-model text is altered by this diff. Because no code was supplied, the claims above are unverified. A threat-model update may be needed for the dev/prod coexistence and shared APNs app identity limitation (TB-011) if the code lands separately.
